question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 2 & -6\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}} & -\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A,$ $Σ,$ and $V$ shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ what is the second column of $U?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ and ${\sigma }_{i}\ne 0,$ then the $i$th column of $U$ can be found as

$$
{u}_{i}=\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{i}}A{v}_{i},
$$

 

where ${v}_{i}$ is the $i$th column of the matrix $V.$

From the matrix $Σ,$ we deduce that the singular values are ${\sigma }_{1}=7$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=6.$ Therefore, the second column of $U$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{2} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{2}}A{v}_{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 2 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}-\frac{12}{\sqrt{13}} \\ -\frac{18}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}} \\ -\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
